title: Pairwise independence of the resolution base-change maps
statement: For f:X→S, g:S′→S with g and g′ flat, an O_X-module F and p≥0, any two injective-resolution pairs (I,J), (I₁,J₁), with augmented lifts t and t₁ of the unit of g′^*, give the same flatBaseChangeResolutionBeta. The construction is that of [def-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-resolution-construction]; resolutions and lifts have exactly the augmentation equation of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-lift].

proof.text: Use InjectiveResolution.homotopyEquiv to obtain augmented comparison maps a : I → I₁ and b : J → J₁. Flatness of g′ makes the terms of g′_*J₁ injective. The augmentation equations show that t followed by g′_*b and a followed by t₁ agree on F in degree zero. Construct their homotopy directly over the natural numbers: for their difference e, exactness of F → I⁰ → I¹ extends e⁰ to s₀ : I¹ → (g′_*J₁)⁰; exactness in each successive degree extends eⁿ - s_{n-1}d to s_n. The chain-map equation makes this difference vanish on the preceding differential. Mathlib Homotopy.mkCoinductive assembles these extensions. This is the private proved helper augmentedHomotopy, which needs no exactness of the target complex.

Map this homotopy by f_* and compose with the natural square isomorphism. Naturality of that isomorphism gives the homotopy between q followed by g_*f′_*b and f_*a followed by q₁. Apply g^* and compose with the termwise counit. Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_right_symm and homEquiv_naturality_left_symm identify the endpoints with c followed by f′_*b and g^*f_*a followed by c₁. Homotopy.homologyMap_eq gives equality of the induced cohomology composites.

Apply InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj_hom_naturality to a over the identity of F, and isoRightDerivedObj_inv_naturality to b over the identity of g′^*F. Apply ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso_inv_naturality to f_*a and the exact functor g^*. Expand flatBaseChangeResolutionBeta. Substitute the source comparison, move it through the pullback-homology isomorphism, use the equality on homology from the preceding step, and cancel the target comparison by inverse naturality. The resulting composites are exactly the asserted two maps.

lean.statement:
theorem flatBaseChangeResolutionBeta_independent {X S S' : Scheme.{uBC}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S)
    [Flat g] [Flat (pullback.snd g f)] {F : X.Modules}
    (I : InjectiveResolution F)
    (J : InjectiveResolution ((tensorPullback (pullback.snd g f)).obj F))
    (t : I.cocomplex ⟶ ((pushforward (pullback.snd g f)).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj J.cocomplex)
    (ht : I.ι.f 0 ≫ t.f 0 =
      (Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction (pullback.snd g f))).unit.app F ≫
        (pushforward (pullback.snd g f)).map (J.ι.f 0))
    (I₁ : InjectiveResolution F)
    (J₁ : InjectiveResolution ((tensorPullback (pullback.snd g f)).obj F))
    (t₁ : I₁.cocomplex ⟶ ((pushforward (pullback.snd g f)).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj J₁.cocomplex)
    (ht₁ : I₁.ι.f 0 ≫ t₁.f 0 =
      (Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction (pullback.snd g f))).unit.app F ≫
        (pushforward (pullback.snd g f)).map (J₁.ι.f 0))
    (p : ℕ) :
    flatBaseChangeResolutionBeta f g I J t p =
      flatBaseChangeResolutionBeta f g I₁ J₁ t₁ p
